model_claims.text: parse_header_links splits each Link header parameter on '=' using param.split('=') without maxsplit.
model_claims.source_quote: `parse_header_links` splits each `Link` header parameter on `=` with `key, value = param.split("=")` (no `maxsplit`).

model_claims.text: When a quoted parameter value contains '=', the split creates three or more parts, raising ValueError that is swallowed, causing the parameter and all subsequent ones to be dropped.
model_claims.source_quote: Such a value produces 3+ parts and raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack`, which the bare `except ValueError: break` swallows — silently dropping that parameter **and every parameter after it** in the link.

model_claims.text: In the example, the 'title' parameter is omitted from the parsed links because its value contains an '='.
Changing the split to param.split('=', 1) preserves the '=' inside the value and keeps later parameters.
model_claims.source_quote: `param.split("=")` → `param.split("=", 1)` in `parse_header_links`, so the value keeps its `=` and following parameters are preserved.

model_claims.text: The added test for a value containing '=' fails on main (dropping title and following rel) and passes after the fix.
model_claims.source_quote: Added a `test_parse_header_links` parametrization with a value containing `=` (`title="a=b"` followed by `rel="next"`). It fails on `main` (both `title` and the trailing `rel` are dropped) and passes with the fix.

model_claims.text: No existing issue tracks this bug; it is long‑standing.
model_claims.source_quote: No existing issue tracked this; the bug is long-standing.
